html:
A wave of Buddhist protest in South Vietnam from May to November 1963 against the government of Ngô Đình Diệm, which ended with his overthrow and death.

Diệm was a Catholic ruling a mostly Buddhist country, and Catholics were favoured in jobs, land and the army. In May 1963, on the Buddha's birthday, officials in Huế banned the Buddhist flag. When crowds protested, troops opened fire and nine people died.

Protests spread. On 11 June the monk Thích Quảng Đức sat down at a Saigon crossroads and burned himself to death. A photograph of his calm self-immolation went around the world. In August special forces under his brother raided pagodas across the country and arrested hundreds of monks.

The United States, South Vietnam's main backer, lost patience. It let generals know it would not oppose a coup. On 1 November the army moved, and the next day Diệm and his brother were killed. Years of unstable military rule followed, and American involvement in the Vietnam War grew deeper.
sum: A wave of Buddhist protest in South Vietnam from May to November 1963 against the government of Ngô Đình Diệm, which ended with his overthrow and death.
